title: Layoff Dayroom
oneLiner: A daily command room for laid-off professionals to turn panic, ghosting, and scattered applications into a visible recovery routine.
targetUser: Recently laid-off white-collar workers and career coaches supporting job seekers through long search cycles.
keyUX: Morning check-in chooses the day's search posture, then a board tracks applications, follow-up windows, warm intros, rejection patterns, and one human accountability action.
requiredUISections: Today posture strip: runway, energy, urgency, and confidence.
Application lane board with status, last touch, next action, and ghosting age.
Follow-up clock for recruiters, referrals, and networking asks.
Rejection pattern reader with role, seniority, location, and resume variant.
Accountability room with one small offline or peer action.
Runway-safe task list for benefit paperwork, budget holds, and skill proof.
Weekly recovery report for coach, partner, or support group.
sourceSignalReferences: S3 - Reddit r/Layoffs, live layoff/job-search anxiety
S4 - Reddit r/careerguidance, job search feels 10x harder after layoff
stitchPrompt: Create a polished responsive web app prototype called "Layoff Dayroom" for recently laid-off professionals managing a long job search. The first screen should be the actual daily command room, not a landing page. Include a top posture strip showing runway, energy, urgency, and confidence; an application lane board; follow-up clock; rejection pattern reader; accountability room; runway-safe task list; and weekly recovery report. Use realistic sample data for recruiter ghosting, referral asks, interview loops, and budget pressure. Design direction: use the calm-consumer profile with soft, reassuring surfaces, one gentle accent, steady next actions, readable cards, and no shame-heavy alarm styling.
